primary.key: Shedding the ancient fluid he is poured into the cleansing sieve: He, thundering, hath produced the Gods.
primary.s: The hymn opens with Soma engendering the sun and the lights of heaven, and here turns to the straining of the juice; Sāyaṇa, on 9.42.4, reads his begetting the gods as figurative, since wherever Soma is pressed, there the gods invariably appear.
primary.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa, on Rig Veda 9.42.4, Sanskrit Wikisource, revision 310169 (2021)

basis.words: “क्रन्दन् शब्दं कुर्वन् "देवानजीजनत् जनयति स्वसमीपे । यत्र सोमोऽभिषूयते तत्र देवा नियतं प्रादुर्भवन्ति । अतो जनयतीत्युपचर्यते
basis.gloss: ‘Crying out’: making a sound. ‘He generated the gods’: he generates them near himself. Where Soma is pressed, there the gods invariably become manifest; therefore ‘he generates’ is said figuratively (upacāra).

standby.key: URGED by the men, this vigorous Steed, Lord of the mind, Omniscient, Runs to the woolen straining-cloth.
standby.s: A hymn tracing Soma from the priests’ hands to the vats begins here; Sāyaṇa, on 9.28.1, takes ‘the mind’ as the hymn of praise, or as mind itself, over which Soma presides, citing the scripture in which the moon, becoming mind, entered the heart.
standby.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa, on Rig Veda 9.28.1, Sanskrit Wikisource, revision 208615 (2019)

basis.words: "मनसः स्तोत्रस्य “पतिः स्वामी । अथवा सोमस्य मनोभिमानित्वात् मनसः स्वामित्वं चन्द्रमा मनो भूत्वा हृदयं प्राविशत् ' ( ऐ. आ. २.४.२) इति श्रुतेः
basis.gloss: ‘Of the mind’: of the hymn of praise (stotra); ‘lord’: master. Or else: because Soma is the presiding deity of mind (mano-abhimānin), he is lord of mind, from the scripture ‘the moon, having become mind, entered the heart’ (Aitareya Āraṇyaka 2.4.2).

primary.key: We have accepted thousands from Dhvasra’s and Purusanti’s hands: Swift runs this giver of delight.
primary.s: The hymn’s third verse, before its refrain, names two givers; Sāyaṇa, on 9.58.3, reads it through a Śāṭyāyanaka story of two seers who took much from these kings, felt they had swallowed poison, saw this hymn, and by it made the gain as if unaccepted.
primary.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa, on Rig Veda 9.58.3, Sanskrit Wikisource, revision 403221 (2024)

basis.words: ध्वस्रः कश्चिद्राजा पुरुषन्तिः कश्चित् … अथ ह वै तरन्त पुरुमीळ्हौ वैददश्वी ध्वस्रयोः पुरुषन्त्योर्बहु प्रतिगृह्य गरगिराविव मेनाते तौ ह स्माङ्गुल्या सातं प्रतिममृशाते तावकामयेतामसातं नाविवेदं सातं स्यादात्तमिवैव न प्रतिगृहीतमिति तावेतञ्चतुर्ऋचमपश्यतां तेन प्रत्यैतां ततो वै तयोरसातं सातमभवदात्तमिवैव न प्रतिगृहीतं … तयोरस्माभिः प्रतिगृहीतं तत्सर्वमप्रतिगृहीतमस्त्विति सोमऋषिः प्रार्थयत
basis.gloss: On 9.58.3: Dhvasra is a certain king, Puruṣanti a certain other. … And so the Śāṭyāyanaka: ‘Now Taranta and Purumīḷha, the sons of Vidadaśva, having accepted much from Dhvasra and Puruṣanti, thought themselves like swallowers of poison; they touched the gain with a finger; they wished: may this gain be no gain for us, as though merely taken, not accepted. They saw this four-verse hymn and went back by it; then their gain became no gain, as though merely taken, not accepted.’ … On 9.58.4: the seer prays to Soma that all that was accepted from those two be as not accepted.

standby.key: That he may move, they yoke him to the three-backed triple-seated car By the Seven Rsis’ holy songs.
standby.s: Between verses speeding Soma to battle like a horse, the hymn gives him a chariot; Sāyaṇa, on 9.62.17, reads the car as the sacrifice, its three backs as the three pressings, its three seats as the three Vedas, and the seven songs as seven metres.
standby.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa, on Rig Veda 9.62.17, Sanskrit Wikisource, revision 353481 (2022)

basis.words: “त्रिपृष्ठे त्रिषवणपृष्ठे “त्रिवन्धुरे त्रिवेदवन्धुरे “ऋषीणां “रथे यज्ञरथे “तं सोमं “सप्त सप्तभिः “धीतिभिः छन्दोभिः “यातवे देवान् प्रति गन्तुं “युञ्जन्ति ऋत्विजो योजयन्ति
basis.gloss: ‘Three-backed’: whose backs are the three pressings (savana). ‘Three-seated’: whose seats are the three Vedas. ‘Of the seers’, ‘on the car’: on the chariot of the sacrifice. ‘Him’: Soma. ‘With seven songs’: with the seven metres. ‘That he may move’: to go to the gods. ‘They yoke’: the priests yoke him.
